headline: Wikipedia battles AI-generated content, launching a major cleanup effort
summary: A new WikiProject is tackling the growing challenge of AI-generated text on the platform, aiming to preserve human-written integrity despite detection difficulties.
details: Wikipedia has initiated a significant effort to identify and remove AI-generated content from its vast knowledge base. This proactive measure aims to maintain the encyclopedia's core value of human-authored information and editorial oversight.

The challenge is substantial, as AI-generated text is becoming increasingly sophisticated and harder for human editors to distinguish from authentic writing. Despite these difficulties, the cleanup project is actively underway.

Cofounded by Ellia Lebleu, the WikiProject AI Cleanup effort focuses on preserving the integrity and reliability of Wikipedia. The initiative underscores the community's commitment to ensuring that the platform remains a trusted source of human-curated knowledge.

topic: ai agents as new media audience
headline_marked: [[Media outlets are now creating content for AI agents]], shifting how news is consumed
headline: Media outlets are now creating content for AI agents, shifting how news is consumed
summary: Major publishers like Axios are creating dedicated feeds for AI agents, while others like Every are embedding AI prompts directly into articles, signaling a foundational shift in news consumption.
details: Some news outlets are fundamentally changing their content strategy, now creating articles specifically for AI agents rather than solely for human readers. This trend is emerging as individuals increasingly use AI agents for personalized news briefings, like Michelle Seo's daily updates from her Muse AI agent, Chattiana.

Axios Chief Revenue Officer Jacquelyn Cameron notes a significant shift in the media ecosystem. She points to the deterioration of the open web, shrinking search, and the surge in hyperpersonalization driven by Large Language Models (LLMs) as key factors.

In response, Axios announced 'Axios Direct,' a series of feeds explicitly designed for AI agents. These feeds prioritize structured data over narrative, aiming to be a more efficient way for agents to access content, akin to a Bloomberg terminal.

The first two Axios Direct feeds target corporate clients. One, launched this fall, provides AI agents of Axios Pro Deals subscribers with access to merger-and-acquisition content. The second, launching next year, will serve as a source to train in-house LLMs.

Axios also plans a third, consumer-facing Axios Direct feed for individual subscribers next year, allowing their AI agents to receive Axios reporting directly. All three feeds will be standardized text, not designed for human aesthetic consumption.

Every, another tech media and software company, is taking a different approach by integrating AI prompts directly into its articles. This allows readers to interact with and test concepts using AI as an extension of themselves.

Every's articles often include buttons like 'Read With Claude' or 'Read With ChatGPT,' which generate prompts for AI to summarize content or delve deeper. This strategy enables writers to pack stories with extensive details, confident that AI agents can extract the most relevant information for readers.
